verdict.rationale: Turso documents per-user and per-agent database provisioning through its Platform API: you create, token-scope and tear down each isolated database. It also ships fleet management of databases, groups and tokens, and automated branching that creates a database for each pull request (previews). The 'thousands or millions' scale claim and low cost rest mainly on vendor marketing, with only an anecdotal community note that it is cheap. missing for 10: documented per-database pricing or limits proving cheapness at thousands of databases, independent hands-on corroboration of fleet-scale provisioning, a published OpenAPI spec (probe returned 404).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can cheaply create thousands of isolated databases — one per agent, tenant, or preview — and manage the fleet programmatically

citations.quote: Provision a dedicated database per user or per AI agent. Each entity gets its own isolated SQLite database that you create, token-scope, and tear down via the API.
Spin up thousands or millions of isolated databases programmatically, each with its own boundary.
Programmatically manage databases, groups, organizations, and tokens with the Turso Platform API.
Automating branching is useful for creating a new database for each pull request.
Spin a database for every user, agent, and tenant.
Super fast and cheap, haven't had to need more than the free tier.
